summary: Saved filter sharing applies org-scoped trace hooks to unintended projects, exposing trace links
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports that when a user in their org saves a dashboard filter and shares it with a team, tracehook links attached to panels are becoming visible in other projects that should not have access. Impact: Potential exposure of trace links and context across projects within the same org and occasionally to members of partner tenant projects after a recent saved-filter sharing change. Environment: prod us-west and eu-west, console v2.14.2, tracehook service tag v2026-03-10.

Observed behavior:
- Saved filter created in Project A with a tracehook attached appears in Project B when that filter is shared with team "DataInfra".
- Clicking the dashboard panel in Project B opens trace links that resolve to traces from Project A.

Expected behavior: Shared saved filters should preserve project-scoped tracehook tokens and not surface links to traces outside the viewer's project scope.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) In org 'datawave', create Project A and Project B with two separate dashboards.
2) In Project A create a dashboard panel and attach a tracehook (project-scoped) via the panel's saved filter.
3) Save the filter and use the 'share' action to share it with team 'DataInfra' (team includes members of Project B).
4) Log in as a member of Project B, open the shared saved filter and apply to a dashboard panel in Project B.
5) Click the panel's trace link -> observe trace details from Project A visible in Project B UI.
6) Verify access via API: call /api/trace/{traceid} from a Project B API key and receive 200 + full trace payload for Project A trace (should be 403).

comments: Leah Park (Support): Customer reported at 2026-03-12 18:10 UTC. They flagged this as urgent because traces contain internal IDs. Asked for immediate triage and mitigation.

Samir Patel (SRE): Acknowledged and assigned. Initial hypothesis: permission token used by saved-filter share flow is not namespacing the token to project scope after the 2.14.2 UI change. Reproduced locally in staging with a small repro script.
Customer (Jane Liu, DataWave): "We only share filters with our infra team, not other projects. This looks like a regression after last week's console update. Please advise mitigation steps."
Samir Patel (SRE): Temporarily revoked saved-filter sharing for DataWave org and rotated tracehook keys. Will follow up with rollback/patch plan.
investigation_notes: Repro confirmed in staging: saved filter share flow calls sharing-service which previously returned project-scoped hook metadata; new UI patch stores only hook id and a global token, causing service to resolve hook using caller project context rather than original project scope.
Auth logs show trace-service accepts API lookup requests based on token presence but does not validate original hook owner project after the UI change introduced a 'global' token mode.
Related PR identified that touched saved-filter serialization: PR #4302 (console) added optimism for shared-filters and inadvertently dropped project_id from hook envelope.
No evidence of external tenant cross-org leak; exposure limited to members within the same Redwood org who had access to shared filters.
resolution: In progress - hotfix branch created to restore project_id into saved-filter hook envelope and to enforce project validation in trace-service. Patch planned for 2026-03-14 canary deploy to us-west with feature-flag disabled-by-default. Will roll forward upon verification.
workaround:
1) Disable saved-filter sharing at org level for affected orgs (console: Organization Settings -> Sharing -> disable).
2) Rotate tracehook tokens for sensitive projects per runbook.
3) Temporary ACL applied: trace-service set to enforce project-owner check for all incoming hook resolution requests (rate-limited emergency guard).
root_cause: Regression introduced in console v2.14.2 where saved-filter sharing serialization dropped project scoping for attached tracehooks; trace-service did not have a defensive validation for hook owner project when resolving hook ids issued via shared filters.
follow_up_tasks: 1) Deploy hotfix to us-west canary and verify with DataWave staging repro (owner: Samir).
2) Add integration test that asserts saved-filter share payloads retain hook owner project id (owner: QE).
3) Enhance trace-service to require project-owner header when resolving a tracehook and return 403 if mismatch (owner: Platform).
4) Communicate to impacted customers with mitigation steps and token rotation guidance (owner: CS).
5) Postmortem + update runbook for saved-filter sharing (owner: Support Ops).
